title: The GUM's Type B evaluation uses means other than the statistical analysis of a series of observations
summary: The GUM's Type B evaluation uses means other than the statistical analysis of a series of observations.
body: The Guide defines a Type B evaluation as a method of evaluating uncertainty by means other than the statistical analysis of a series of observations. The source says: "observations 2.3.3 Type B evaluation (of uncertainty) method of evaluation of uncertainty by means other than the statistical analysis of series of observations 2.3.4 combined standard uncertainty standard uncertainty of the result of a measurement when that result is obtained from the values of a number of other quantities, equal to the positive square root of a sum of terms, the terms being the variances or covariances of these other quantities weighted according to h" A number taken from a calibration certificate or a prior bound can be a Type B input. It is still an uncertainty component. It is not a second-class guess merely because it did not come from repeating the measurement.
said_by: Joint Committee for Guides in Metrology
